items.title: Mitchel McAllister Interview, 1960-03-19
items.q: The first one came in here was the colored fellow by the name of Frank Brakely. He played trombone.

ctx.x: Ooh, 78. You've got a right good age, huh? Did they have any trumpets or clarinets or saxophones or trombones when you were young?

No, sir. The first one came in here was the colored fellow by the name of Frank Brakely. He played trombone. Trombone was first. Then the little short cornet. And then people began to add sax. And Bud's son, I know he ran away from the band at one time, and he decided he would, he thought within himself that he would learn to play sax. And he got on his father and warned him to learn him sax. To buy him a sax, at least. And his father gave him a sax. And he was just, he mastered that for just, he wasn't a month.
He was reading a little, and he got to be a perfect wizard on that side.
